description: Deterministic values parity mode injects into the adapters (adapters) and the user sync code (server_sites) that read the wall clock or a random source. They are installed process-wide at startup when parity.enabled is true (Go: parity/fakes.Install from parity/wiring.Bootstrap) and set per case from envelope.fakes (omitted or zero fields take these defaults). Outside parity mode every seam behaves exactly like the original code. The clock is a fixed instant whose location is UTC; code that explicitly converts to local time (huaweiads getClientTime .Local()) depends on the process time zone, so the runner starts both servers with TZ=UTC. The Rust server must inject the same values at the same sites.

generated_uuids.description: In parity mode every random v4 UUID the server generates (Go: every uuid.NewV4 in the process) is drawn from this deterministic stream instead. Go generates them on the request path for {{UUID}} request ids, source.tid and imp[].ext.tid, generated bid ids and cache keys. The differ still numbers them with <uuid#n> placeholders, but a placeholder cannot reach inside a gzip-compressed bidder request: random tids change the compressed length, so without the stream two Go processes send different Content-Length headers for the same case. The stream restarts whenever the fake values are set: at the start and at the end of every case, and on /__parity/reset. Concurrent draws get distinct values from the same stream, in draw order.
generated_uuids.algorithm: The n-th UUID (n = 1, 2, ...) is the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of seed + ":" + n in decimal, with byte 6 set to (byte6 & 0x0f) | 0x40 (version 4) and byte 8 set to (byte8 & 0x3f) | 0x80 (RFC 4122 variant), written as lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 hex.

orders.name: bidder_request_phase
orders.order: The bidders of one auction build their requests one at a time in bidder name order: a bidder's bidder-request hook stage and MakeRequests start after MakeRequests of every bidder before it returned (or its goroutine ended), and HTTP calls and MakeBids still run concurrently. Values an adapter writes through objects its request shares with other bidders' requests reach the bidders after it, as when Go schedules them in that order. Without a parity case, with one bidder, or with a repeated bidder name the bidders run freely.
